podcast.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis Journey
podcast.body: In his early 20s, Dan Reynolds began experiencing intense lower back pain and a gradual loss of mobility, making walking, standing, and singing painful, despite no apparent injury. After consulting a series of doctors over a year without a clear answer, he finally saw a rheumatologist who diagnosed him with ankylosing spondylitis, a condition he had never heard of but resolved to fight from the outset. "Finally, though, he saw a rheumatologist, and he came back with the diagnosis of end-collossing spondylitis."

podcast.title: Mormon Missionary Service
podcast.body: At the age of 19, Dan Reynolds, the singer for Imagine Dragons, served for two years as a Mormon missionary. This period of his life preceded his musical career with the band. "Dan Reynolds, the singer for Imagine Dragons, worked as a Mormon missionary for two years when he turned 19."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Treatment and Advocacy Efforts
podcast.body: Dan Reynolds is currently managing his ankylosing spondylitis through a treatment plan involving exercise, diet, and medication, which allows him to live relatively pain-free and pursue a full life. He is actively involved in raising awareness and funds for the condition, engaging with the AS patient community through the website amonsterpainintheAS.com and collaborating with the pharmaceutical company Novartis to develop new treatments. "This is something I'm going to live with for the rest of my life, because there is no current cure."

xref.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis and Songwriting
xref.body: Singer Dan Reynolds suffers from Ankylosing Spondylitis, a type of arthritis that affects the joints of the spine, hips, and shoulders, causing increasing stiffness and pain. He channeled this personal struggle into the song "Believer," writing it as a self-motivational pep talk. "Dan Reynolds suffers from a type of arthritis called Enkelosing Spondylitis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Berkeley School of Music Influence
xref.body: Three out of the four current members of Imagine Dragons (Wayne Sermon, Ben McKee, and Daniel Platzman) are graduates or students of the Berkeley School of Music, indicating a strong academic musical background within the band. "That leaves us with today's Imagine Dragons lineup. Dan Reynolds, Wayne Sermon, Ben McKee, and Daniel Platsman, three of them, Berkeley School of Music students."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dan Reynolds' Professional Drive
xref.body: Despite being a great student with discipline who could have pursued a business career, Dan Reynolds realized he had to be a professional musician and dedicated all his energy and focus to this path. "He realized that he had to be a professional musician. So he put all his energies, all his focus, and all his discipline into that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life of Dan Reynolds
xref.body: Singer Dan Reynolds was born seventh in a nine-child Mormon family in Las Vegas. He was an Eagle Scout, quarterback of his high school team, and served as a full-time missionary for two years in his late teens, during which he was allowed only two phone calls home per year (Mother's Day and Christmas). "He was born seventh in a nine child Mormon family in Las Vegas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding at Brigham Young University
xref.body: Imagine Dragons was formed in 2008 while singer Dan Reynolds was an excellent student at Brigham Young University, where he also met early members like drummer Andrew Tolman. "And this is where Imagine Dragons was formed. This was 2008."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: LGBTQ+ Activism
xref.body: Dan Reynolds became an outspoken activist for LGBTQ+ rights, despite being a straight, married former Mormon missionary with three children. He heads the LoveLoud foundation and music festival, which has raised over a million dollars for LGBTQ+-related organizations. He openly displays a rainbow flag at shows, even in risky regions like Turkey and Utah, where the Mormon church has differing views, and has prompted statements from the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Shortly after the evolve album came out, we started hearing about Dan Reynolds' activism for LGBTQ rights."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Most Famous Mormon in Music
xref.body: Dan Reynolds is considered by some to be the most famous Mormon in music currently, and his activism has put pressure on the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, compelling them to issue statements regarding his public comments and actions. "After all, it is possible that Dan is the most famous Mormon in music right now."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
